newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador refinery shut down to start July 5.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador refinery shut down to start July 5.

text.p: The shutdown of Ecuador's largest oil refinery will start July 5 and last for a month and a half, an official from state-owned oil company Petroecuador said Tuesday.

"The planned shutdown starts July 5 and will last 45 days, during which the necessary oil imports for internal consumption will take place," a Petroecuador official who asked not to be named told Reuters.

The scheduled shutdown of the Esmeraldas refinery is due to work to modernize the plant. Once completed at the end of 1997, the refinery's upgrade is hoped to lift production to 110,000 barrels daily from 90,000 barrels currently.
The shutdown will lead to production loss of four million barrels of crude which would be the amount that would be refined in the 45 days, the official said.
Ecuador, one of Latin America's largest oil producers, operates three refinaries.

Esmeraldas, north-west of Quito, produced 8.11 million barrels in the first quarter, of which 3.15 million barrels of diesel and 264,000 barrels of gasoline were exported. It has a refining cost of $1.74 per barrel.
